ei.title: Chapter 0-QN23~24 1번: Market Incentives and Ecosystem Services
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that ①<u>provide</u> financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands ②<u>have</u> a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus ③<u>is</u> unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may ④<u>exceed</u> the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: is → are: 주어 These services가 복수이므로 복수 동사 are가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
① provide — 관계대명사 that의 선행사 market incentives(복수) → provide 정상
② have — 주어 owners(복수), have a market incentive 정상
③ is — 원문 are, 주어 These services(복수)이므로 are 필수 ←정답
④ exceed — 조동사 may 뒤 동사원형 exceed 정상
det.tip: 복수 주어(These services) → 복수 동사(are). 단수 is는 비문

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that ①<u>provides</u> financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than ②<u>manage</u> the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits ③<u>provided</u> by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not ④<u>sending</u> the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: provides → provide: 관계대명사 that의 선행사 market incentives가 복수이므로 provide가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
① provides — 원문 provide, 관계대명사 that의 선행사 market incentives(복수) → provide 필수 ←정답
② manage — to cut down ~ rather than (to) manage, to부정사 병렬구조 정상
③ provided — the benefits (which are) provided by services, 과거분사 정상
④ sending — markets are not sending, 현재진행형 정상
det.tip: 관계대명사 that절의 동사는 선행사(incentives, 복수)에 수일치 → provide

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to ①<u>influence</u> management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, ②<u>based</u> on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times ③<u>greater</u> per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not ④<u>send</u> the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: send → sending: be동사(are) + not + 현재분사(sending)의 진행형 구조이므로 sending이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
① influence — be unlikely to + 동사원형(influence), to부정사 정상
② based — (which is) based on their non-market values, 과거분사 정상
③ greater — over three times greater ~ than, 비교급 정상
④ send — 원문 sending, markets are not sending, be동사 뒤 현재분사 필수 ←정답
det.tip: be + not + V-ing = 진행형. are not send는 비문, are not sending

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands ①<u>have</u> a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits ②<u>providing</u> by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times ③<u>greater</u> per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to ④<u>favor</u> ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: providing → provided: economic benefits는 '제공되는' 대상이므로 수동의 과거분사 provided가 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
① have — 주어 owners(복수), have a market incentive 정상
② providing — 원문 provided, the economic benefits (which are) provided by services, 이익은 '제공받는' 대상이므로 수동 과거분사 필수 ←정답
③ greater — three times greater than, 비교급 정상
④ favor — to favor ecosystem services, to부정사 정상
det.tip: 명사 뒤 분사: 능동관계면 V-ing, 수동관계면 p.p. benefits는 제공되므로 provided

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial ①<u>rewards</u> for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than ②<u>manage</u> the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are ③<u>likely</u> to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate ④<u>regulation</u>, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ likely(~하기 쉬운): 서비스가 재정적 이익을 주지 '않으므로' 관리 결정에 영향을 미치기 '어렵다(unlikely)'가 맞다. likely는 논리 모순.
det.analysis:
① rewards(보상) — 시장 유인이 재정적 보상을 제공 — 적절
② manage(관리하다) — 나무를 베는 것과 대조되는 숲 관리 — 적절
③ likely(~하기 쉬운) — 원문 unlikely. 재정적 이익이 없으므로 관리 결정에 영향을 미치기 어려움(unlikely), likely는 반대 ←정답
④ regulation(조절) — 기후 조절은 생태계 서비스의 예 — 적절
det.tip: unlikely(~할 것 같지 않은) ↔ likely(~하기 쉬운). 앞 절 'no financial benefits'와 인과가 맞아야 함

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon ①<u>capture</u>, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic ②<u>value</u> of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per ③<u>hectare</u> than the market benefits. Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the ④<u>wrong</u> "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ wrong(잘못된): 시장이 생태계 서비스를 선호하도록 '올바른(correct)' 신호를 보내지 못한다는 맥락이므로 correct가 맞다. wrong은 문맥 모순.
det.analysis:
① capture(포집) — 탄소 포집은 생태계 서비스의 예 — 적절
② value(가치) — 목재의 경제적 가치 — 적절
③ hectare(헥타르) — 헥타르당 이익 비교 단위 — 적절
④ wrong(잘못된) — 원문 correct. 시장이 보내지 못하는 것은 '올바른' 신호(correct signal), wrong은 반대 ←정답
det.tip: correct signal = 올바른 신호. 시장이 이 correct 신호를 못 보내 벌목이 조장됨

questions.stem: 산림 소유주들은 숲을 보존하기보다 나무를 벰으로써 재정적 보상을 얻을 수 있다.

det.korean: T: 본문 'market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation'와 'a market incentive to cut down trees'에서 벌목이 재정적 보상으로 이어짐을 확인.
det.analysis: 본문: managers face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation + owners have a market incentive to cut down trees → 나무를 베면 재정적 보상. T.
det.tip: exploitation(개발/착취) = cut down trees = 재정적 보상의 원천

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. questions.stem: UN의 한 계획에 따르면, 목재의 시장 이익이 열대림 생태계 서비스의 경제적 이익보다 더 크다.

det.korean: F: 본문 'the economic benefits of ecosystem services ~ are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits' → 생태계 서비스 이익이 시장(목재) 이익보다 세 배 더 크다. 진술은 반대.
det.analysis: 본문: ecosystem services 이익이 market benefits보다 over three times greater. 진술은 목재 시장 이익이 더 크다고 했으므로 관계 역전. F.
det.tip: 비교 방향 주의: 생태계 서비스 > 시장 이익 (세 배). 진술은 거꾸로

Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to favor ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 생태계 서비스는 산림 소유주에게 직접적인 재정적 이익을 제공하여 관리 결정에 큰 영향을 미친다.

det.korean: F: 본문 'These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions' → 재정적 이익을 주지 못하며 관리 결정에 영향을 미치기 어렵다. 진술은 반대.
det.analysis: 본문: no financial benefits + unlikely to influence management decisions → 재정적 이익 없음, 영향 거의 없음. 진술은 '직접 이익 제공, 큰 영향'이라 반대. F.
det.tip: no financial benefits = 재정적 이익 없음 → unlikely to influence

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to __________ trees rather than manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. For example, a United Nations initiative has estimated that the economic benefits of ecosystem services provided by tropical forests, including climate regulation, water purification, and erosion prevention, are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 시장 유인은 숲을 관리(manage)하기보다 나무를 '베는(cut down)' 쪽으로 작용한다. exploitation(개발)에 재정적 보상이 주어지기 때문이다.
det.analysis:
① cut down(베어 넘기다) — rather than manage와 대조, 착취(exploitation)에 보상이 주어지는 흐름과 일치 ←정답
② care for(돌보다) — 숲을 돌보는 것은 manage 쪽이라 유인 방향과 반대
③ fully restore(완전히 복원하다) — 복원은 보존 행위, 시장 유인과 반대
④ carefully protect(신중히 보호하다) — 보호도 보존 행위라 문맥 모순
det.tip: 시장 유인은 exploitation(개발)에 보상 → 나무를 cut down. manage/protect는 그 반대

questions.passage: Managers of natural resources typically face market incentives that provide financial rewards for exploitation. For example, owners of forest lands have a market incentive to cut down trees __________ manage the forest for carbon capture, wildlife habitat, flood protection, and other ecosystem services. These services provide the owner with no financial benefits, and thus are unlikely to influence management decisions. But the economic benefits provided by these services, based on their non-market values, may exceed the economic value of the timber. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소유주는 숲을 '관리하기보다(rather than manage)' 나무를 벨 유인을 가진다. 벌목과 관리가 대조되는 관계이므로 rather than이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
① in order to(~하기 위해) — 목적 표현이라 '베는 목적이 관리'라는 이상한 뜻이 됨
② so as to(~하기 위해) — 역시 목적 표현이라 문맥 모순
③ rather than(~하기보다) — cut down과 manage가 대조되는 선택 관계 ←정답
④ as well as(~뿐만 아니라) — 벌목과 관리를 동시에 한다는 뜻이라 유인 방향과 안 맞음
det.tip: cut down trees ↔ manage the forest, 두 선택을 대조 → rather than

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 일치: 본문 'the economic benefits of ecosystem services ~ are over three times greater per hectare than the market benefits'.
det.analysis:
① 불일치 — These services provide the owner with no financial benefits
② 불일치 — 생태계 서비스가 시장 이익보다 세 배 큼(관계 역전)
③ 불일치 — markets are NOT sending the correct signal
④ 일치 — 생태계 서비스 이익이 헥타르당 목재 시장 이익을 초과 ←정답
det.tip: 숫자·비교 방향(세 배, 초과)과 부정어(no, not)에 유의

ch: 생태계 서비스는 산림 소유주에게 즉각적인 재정적 보상을 제공한다.
UN 계획에 따르면 목재의 시장 가치가 생태계 서비스보다 세 배 더 크다.

열대림 생태계 서비스의 경제적 이익은 헥타르당 목재의 시장 이익을 초과할 수 있다.

나무를 베는 것은 경제적으로 비효율적이라고 평가된다.

Thus cutting down the trees is economically inefficient, and markets are not sending the correct "signal" to ④<u>favor</u> ecosystem services over extractive uses.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: what → that/which: 사물 선행사 market incentives를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사는 that 또는 which이다. what은 선행사를 포함하므로 불가.
det.analysis:
① what — 원문 that, 선행사 market incentives(사물)를 받는 주격 관계대명사는 that/which 필수. what은 선행사 포함이라 불가 ←정답
② have — 주어 owners(복수) have 정상
③ provided — the benefits (which are) provided by services, 과거분사 정상
④ favor — to favor ecosystem services, to부정사 정상
det.tip: 선행사 있는 관계대명사 = that/which. what은 the thing which(선행사 포함)라 뒤에 명사 선행사와 못 씀
